Events

1. What are Ignite Events?
  • Ignite generates events for various operations: cache operations, task executions, topology changes, discovery events, etc.;
  • Events are disabled by default for performance — you must explicitly enable the event types you need;
  • You can listen for events locally or remotely;
2. Enabling Events
  • Enable specific event types in the configuration: 
    IgniteConfiguration cfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
cfg.setIncludeEventTypes(
    EventType.EVT_CACHE_OBJECT_PUT,
    EventType.EVT_CACHE_OBJECT_READ,
    EventType.EVT_CACHE_OBJECT_REMOVED,
    EventType.EVT_NODE_JOINED,
    EventType.EVT_NODE_LEFT,
    EventType.EVT_NODE_FAILED
);
  • Only enable the events you actually need — each enabled event type adds overhead;
3. Local Event Listeners
  • Listen for events on the local node: 
    ignite.events().localListen(event -> {
    CacheEvent cacheEvent = (CacheEvent) event;
    System.out.printf("Cache op: %s, key: %s%n",
        cacheEvent.type(), cacheEvent.key());
    return true; // return true to continue listening
}, EventType.EVT_CACHE_OBJECT_PUT, EventType.EVT_CACHE_OBJECT_REMOVED);
4. Remote Event Listeners
  • Listen for events on remote nodes — useful for monitoring from a client: 
    // Remote filter runs on each node (filters events)
IgnitePredicate<CacheEvent> remoteFilter = event ->
    event.cacheName().equals("importantCache");

// Local listener runs on the client (receives filtered events)
IgnitePredicate<CacheEvent> localListener = event -> {
    System.out.println("Remote event: " + event.type());
    return true;
};

ignite.events().remoteListen(
    localListener,
    remoteFilter,
    EventType.EVT_CACHE_OBJECT_PUT
);
5. Common Event Types
CategoryEvent Types
CacheEVT_CACHE_OBJECT_PUT, EVT_CACHE_OBJECT_READ, EVT_CACHE_OBJECT_REMOVED, EVT_CACHE_REBALANCE_STARTED
DiscoveryEVT_NODE_JOINED, EVT_NODE_LEFT, EVT_NODE_FAILED
TaskEVT_TASK_STARTED, EVT_TASK_FINISHED, EVT_TASK_FAILED
JobEVT_JOB_STARTED, EVT_JOB_FINISHED, EVT_JOB_FAILED
